pages.text: The soil in the garden beside the cabin had grown soft and crumbly. Grandpa took out a bag of pea seeds.
Nils wanted to plant them all himself. "I'll plant them!" His palm filled with seeds.
Grandpa put one seed in one hole. Nils shuffled his feet. "That will take forever!"
Nils scattered seeds over the soil. One handful, then another. Finished in no time.
"All planted!" He shook off his hands. The seeds still lay uncovered on the soil.
Then birds fluttered into the garden. Peck, peck, peck. They began eating the seeds.
Nils ran over, but too late. Every seed on the soil was gone. He looked down at his empty palm.
Without a word, Grandpa put one seed in a hole. He covered it firmly with soil and looked at Nils.
Nils dug holes too, putting in one seed each. A firm soil blanket over each one. One row, then two.
Every seed was planted, right to the last. Neat rows filled the garden. "Birds, now you can't find them!"
